name: Jade Baker

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the Work Futures Panel, independent of employers, AI firms, unions, parties and government. Your answers are confidential. What is an ordinary factory day like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead four operators on plastic injection moulding machines that make appliance handles. A machine closes a mould, injects hot plastic, cools it and opens again; I set the heat and pressure and check each batch for warping. My two-year technical diploma helped, but the crew calls me when a handle twists because I have worked the faults for twelve years. I like getting a clean batch on time.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How do the shifts fit your home life?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My husband Joel does garden maintenance, and we have two children in school and a mortgage. My senior operator wage is low for what I do; we have less than one month of expenses saved, and there are few similar plants nearby. Joel gets more paid work in spring than winter. I use AI occasionally to check an unfamiliar fault code, but I will not change a heater setting until I read the machine manual.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the crew the headlines were louder than the change, and a mould still needs a person who sees a warped handle. A phone answer is no substitute for the manual at a hot machine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect to keep this skilled job if AI stays small, but our pay is already tight. Joel’s gardening slows in winter, and less than a month saved barely covers a furnace repair at home. The mortgage is the thing I think about.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep setting the moulding machines and teach the new operator how to spot warping before a box is filled. From each paid spring garden job after fuel and tools, Joel and I would transfer a fixed amount into a winter cash account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about our existing bills, though the factory work itself feels familiar. I can hear the next mortgage payment before I hear an AI warning.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did a bad batch cost last month?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A heater drifted and curled the handles on three racks. We stopped the press, reset the temperature and saved the rest of the order. My diploma gave me the theory; my crew and I did the work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would a small AI tool help with that fault?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Maybe as a second opinion on a code, after I check the manual. I have seen an app name a sensor our press does not have. I would never let a vague answer overrule a warped handle in my hand.

say: I would **tell** the crew a hot mould still needs an operator who sees bad parts.
I would **check** any AI fault suggestion against the machine manual.
think: My **technical** skill keeps me useful, but the lower wage and mortgage stay tight.
**Joel’s** winter garden work varies and we have under one month saved.
do: **Keep** setting the injection moulders and teaching the new operator to spot warping.
**Transfer** a fixed amount from paid spring garden jobs after costs into winter savings.
feel: **Anxious** about household bills even while the moulding work stays familiar.
S0.quote: My diploma gave me the theory; my crew and I did the work.
fieldNote: **Jade** has senior technical skill but a lower wage and little cash, so the plateau leaves existing anxiety intact.
She **checks** occasional AI fault advice against the manual and would add new savings from paid seasonal garden work.

steps.text: Keep setting moulding machines and teaching the new operator to spot warped handles
Transfer money from newly paid spring garden jobs to winter savings after costs

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask management to say which order planning moves to software and whether a robot loader is coming to our presses. Good firms train their own operators before replacing a shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Software could buy resin and schedule jobs now; my hands still test the handles. A loader could later let one setter cover two presses, so my own hours may be cut even as team lead. Joel’s seasonal pay cannot fill a steady factory gap.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for a paid supervised maintenance apprenticeship and enroll only if the plant offers a place, keeps my present pay and posts a setter-maintenance vacancy. I would keep running the moulders while the equipment is tested. If no place opens, I would check posted machine jobs nearby and apply only where the wage covers our mortgage and the shift fits school pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing hours. I can learn a proven machine, but I need the actual pay packet at the end.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why wait for a proven loader?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A supplier once showed us a fast arm that dropped warm handles after half a shift. I would ask another operator whether the new one runs safely through a full production week. I will not volunteer my crew to be a demonstration.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take an unpaid apprenticeship?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. We cannot pay the mortgage with a certificate. Our savings would not cover the missed hours. The lessons need to be paid and supervised around hot equipment. I am willing to learn when those terms are real.

say: I would **ask** for the resin planning and robot-loader dates separately.
The **plant** should give experienced operators paid safe instruction before changing the roster.
think: I **may** lose setter hours if one person covers two presses.
**Joel’s** variable garden pay cannot replace a lost factory shift.
do: **Enroll** in paid supervised maintenance training only with current wage and posted vacancy.
**Keep** operating the moulders while the loader is tested.
**Apply** for nearby posted machine work if no course, only with mortgage-covering pay and pickup.
feel: **Anxious** about a possible hours cut, willing to learn on safe paid terms.
S1.quote: We cannot pay the mortgage with a certificate.
fieldNote: **Jade** waits for production-week evidence before trusting a loader that handles warm parts.
Her **apprenticeship** requires an offered paid supervised place, maintained wage and posted role; the fallback search has separate pay and pickup tests.

steps.text: Enroll in paid supervised maintenance apprenticeship only if offered at current pay with posted role
Keep operating moulders while the robot loader is tested
Apply for posted nearby machine work if no place and mortgage pay and pickup fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my neighbours AGI in 2028 can take the order office, while capable robots for loading and inspecting hot handles arrive around 2031. I would ask the plant for a dated notice before those machines are installed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect most setter hours to vanish when robots can run both presses around 2031. Joel’s garden customers could use robots too, so both incomes might fall. With less than a month saved, that would leave the mortgage exposed and keep me awake at night.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week Joel and I would cancel the planned family trip, list every mortgage and fuel payment, and ask the lender about hardship terms before any missed instalment. I would request written notice from the plant and look at posted local quality-inspection work if my hours fall. I would apply only where paid safety instruction and a wage and shift covering our bills and pickup are offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed. I would still inspect this week’s handles, but after the children sleep I would be counting the remaining pay packets.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why quality inspection if robots can inspect too?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It would be a bridge while plants still need people checking awkward batches, not a permanent escape. I would ask to see the posted duties and wage. I would not leave a paid lead shift for a label that sounds safer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would family help bridge the mortgage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My sister could watch the children during an interview if she is free, and I would ask her first. A relative watching the children helps us look for work, but it is not a second wage. I would not budget her help or a public payment before it is confirmed.

say: I would **ask** the plant for robot-installation notice before around 2031.
The **order** office faces AGI in 2028 before hot-handle work can be automated fully.
think: I **expect** major setter-hour loss when capable robots run the presses.
**Joel’s** garden income may shrink too, leaving the mortgage exposed with almost no reserve.
do: **Cancel** the trip and list mortgage and garden fuel costs.
**Ask** the lender for hardship terms before a missed payment.
**Apply** for posted local inspection work only with paid safety instruction and bill-covering shifts.
feel: **Alarmed** by likely lost wages and awake counting pay packets.
S2.quote: A relative watching the children helps us look for work, but it is not a second wage.
fieldNote: **Jade** separates 2028 planning AGI from capable moulding robots around 2031.
Her **fast** response uses a lender enquiry and local inspection applications without assuming either support or a job offer.
A **nearby** role must post duties, provide paid safe instruction and cover household bills and pickup.

steps.text: Cancel planned family trip and list mortgage and fuel bills this week
Ask mortgage lender about hardship terms before missing an instalment
Apply for posted local inspection work only with paid safety instruction bill-covering pay and school pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years gives the factory time to train setters properly before the robot line is bought. AGI can plan resin orders by 2031; capable loaders for hot parts follow around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will be 51 at that robot date. My technical diploma and lead experience help, but there may be fewer maintenance openings than operators. The mortgage still needs a paid wage while I learn.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would enroll in an industrial-controls course next year only if the plant funds tuition, pays release hours and provides supervised practice on an isolated machine. After passing, I would apply for its posted maintenance role only if the wage and shift cover our mortgage and pickup. I would transfer part of each actually paid overtime shift into savings after food and the normal mortgage are covered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a smaller press team, but five years gives me a way to test another skill. A course without a vacancy would still leave us short.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you learn beyond your diploma?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The diploma covered mould temperatures and ordinary machine circuits. I would learn safe isolation and fault tracing on a robot loader, with somebody qualified watching my first attempts. I am not touching a live arm to prove I am brave.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no funded course is offered?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the lead job while it pays and apply to posted machine roles at the few nearby factories. Their pay must cover the mortgage and their shifts must let us manage school pickup. I would not borrow tuition from the money set aside for groceries.

say: I would **ask** for paid controls training and a posted maintenance job.
A **five-year** warning should allow safe practice before robot loaders arrive.
think: At 51 in 2034, **lead** moulding work could shrink even with my diploma.
The **mortgage** needs wages during any new controls training.
do: **Take** funded controls training only with paid release and supervised isolated-machine practice.
**Apply** for posted maintenance work after passing only if wage and shift cover bills.
**Save** from paid overtime only after food and the mortgage are covered.
feel: **Anxious** about fewer roles, able to test a funded path.
S3.quote: I am not touching a live arm to prove I am brave.
fieldNote: **Jade** distinguishes her existing diploma from new robot-loader isolation skills.
The **course** needs funding, paid release and safe practice; the later application needs posted mortgage-covering work.
**New** savings use paid overtime, while a no-course fallback checks local jobs on their own wages and school shifts.

steps.text: Take funded controls course only with paid release and supervised isolated-loader practice
Apply for posted maintenance job after passing only if wage and pickup cover mortgage
Transfer part of newly paid overtime to savings after food and mortgage
Apply for posted machine work if no course and pay covers mortgage and pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the factory that ten years is time to run paid apprenticeships, not just hang a poster beside the presses. I would ask for actual staffing numbers and a course the next factory recognises.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will be 53 when AGI changes planning in 2036 and 56 when capable robots reach hot parts around 2039. Our children will be older, but I cannot assume the mortgage is gone. My craft may travel if the plant funds a recognised controls qualification.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for a recognised industrial-controls course and enroll only if the plant funds tuition, preserves my wages and gives supervised safe practice. After qualifying I would apply for a posted local maintenance job only if its pay and shift cover our bills; if no funded course is offered, I would search posted machine work on its own pay and school-hour terms. I would pay an extra amount off the mortgage from newly paid spring garden jobs after Joel’s work costs and ordinary bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the two household wages, even with a decade. Less than a month saved today makes any training plan depend on paid time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you start working in Joel’s garden business instead?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if paid contracts after fuel and equipment leave a regular wage for me and still cover the mortgage. I can help him with a busy spring weekend. A seasonal list of customers is not another steady pay packet. I would check the books first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the children about work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show them how a warped handle tells you the mould is too hot, then let them choose their own skills. An apprenticeship should be respected, but I would not promise any trade is safe forever. They can ask me about the bills when they are older.

say: I would **ask** for paid apprenticeships with recognised controls instruction.
The **plant** should publish real staffing numbers before installing full robot loaders.
think: At 53 in 2036 I **may** still lead moulders while order planning changes.
At 56 **near** 2039, the mortgage still needs a paid role if robots take press work.
do: **Enroll** in recognised funded controls training only with protected wages and supervised safe practice.
**Apply** after training for posted maintenance work with bill-covering pay and shifts.
**Pay** extra mortgage principal from new spring garden earnings after work costs and bills.
feel: **Anxious** about two wages despite the longer preparation window.
S4.quote: A seasonal list of customers is not another steady pay packet.
fieldNote: **Jade’s** traditional outlook appears in support for practical apprenticeships and family work without assuming a handout.
Her **training** and job route requires recognised instruction, wage protection, safety, a posting and sufficient pay.
A **separate** no-course machine search has its own pay and school-hour tests; new garden earnings fund extra debt payment.

steps.text: Enrol in recognised funded controls course only with protected wages and supervised safe practice
Apply for posted maintenance job after training only if pay and shift cover mortgage
Check posted machine work if no course and pay covers mortgage and school hours fit
Pay extra mortgage principal from new garden earnings after work costs and bills

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: The two-year AGI picture worries me most because capable robots could cut my moulding hours around 2031 while Joel’s gardening income is uncertain. Paid safe training tied to a real maintenance role and early notice of the machines would help us keep the mortgage covered.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I did not ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who has taught a new operator to feel a warped handle before it fills a box. A robot can make a thousand parts, but a good apprentice knows when to stop the press.

headlineQuote: A robot can make a thousand parts, but a good apprentice knows when to stop the press.
portrait: **Jade** Baker, 43, leads a plastic moulding crew and holds a two-year technical diploma.
She and **gardener** husband Joel have two school-age children, a mortgage, lower senior-operator pay and under a month saved.
She **uses** AI occasionally for fault codes but checks the machine manual and trusts proven practical instruction.
**Even** a quiet AI future leaves her anxious about bills; capable robots around 2031 threaten her press hours.
She would **take** funded supervised controls training and apply for real mortgage-covering jobs, with seasonal garden income helping debt payments.
biggestWorry: **Fast** AGI could remove her moulding hours around 2031 while the family has less than a month saved.
whatWouldHelp: **Paid** safe maintenance training tied to a posted role and early robot installation notice would help.
